A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MixFlow-MG research. All 19 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, code listings, and appendices, support reliable comparison despite relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original memory and runtime benchmarks, model-scaling experiments, and component ablations, including Figures 1–11 and Tables 2–3.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmarking and ablation results in the main text and appendices. Retained results still qualify as original empirical work.

M1.justification: The reparameterization, mixed-mode differentiation, block rematerialization, and saved inner gradients are unchanged. The added PyTorch listing documents the same intended algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic motivating example and Chinchilla language-modeling setups for learning rates, MAML, and adaptive loss weighting. No evaluated dataset, task, or domain is added or removed.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain standard reverse-over-reverse Truncated-BPTT and the same optimization variants. Newly cited implicit-gradient methods are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The JAX benchmarks, H100/TPUv5p hardware, memory and runtime metrics, and configuration sweeps remain unchanged, including Tables 1 and 4–6. The PyTorch listing does not introduce a reported PyTorch experiment.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Figures 3 and 10 and Tables 2–3 are retained, alongside the same model, batch-size, sequence-length, and inner-update sensitivity analyses. Calling Figure 3 an ablation study in v2 does not add an analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The configuration-sweep reporting and seed parameter in the motivating-example code are unchanged.

E6.justification: The plotted results and numerical table entries are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains the fully optimized 489M results of 54.8 GiB/5.45 seconds on GPU and 46.9 GiB/4.12 seconds on TPU. Added prose about inner-loop-length invariance describes the existing Figure 5 trend.

T1.justification: The stated reverse-mode computational cost changes from O(T|theta|) in v1 Section 2.2 to O(|eta|) + O(T|theta|) in v2 Section 2.3. Proposition 3.1, the derivative identities, appendix derivations, and memory-scaling relation otherwise retain their mathematical content.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains efficient exact bilevel-gradient computation through mixed-mode differentiation. The headline memory and runtime improvement claims are retained; additional emphasis and the PyTorch implementation mention do not redefine the scientific claims.

C2.justification: The explanations involving saved activations, memory-buffer reuse, and compiler behavior remain, as do hardware-dependent performance caveats and static-memory limitations. The expanded background largely reorganizes existing interpretations.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix A.3 adds a PyTorch implementation as Code Listing 2 alongside the retained JAX code. However, its backward function references loss, which is undefined within the listing, instead of the supplied inner_loss_fn. Existing benchmark details are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Calian et al. (2025), Rajeswaran et al. (2019), and Lorraine et al. (2020), removes Lu et al. (2022), and explicitly distinguishes implicit from forward-mode approximations. The overall positioning as an exact-gradient computational improvement remains.

P1.justification: The main structural edit moves and expands v1 Appendix A.1 into v2 Section 2.2, with the BLO discussion becoming Section 2.3. Other changes include local prose revisions, condensed author contributions, updated acknowledgements, and removal of the generic Impact Statement; the overall method-and-experiment narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: Several existing displays are relocated, including Figures 1, 7, and 8 and Table 1. v2 adds a code-listing block and reformats the autodiff primer's equations, while retaining all plotted content, table structures, axes, and legends.

improvement.justification: Moving and expanding the autodiff primer before the method improves accessibility, while the added citations and complexity refinement provide modest clarification. The PyTorch example broadens implementation guidance, although its undefined loss reference limits immediate usability. The empirical support remains unchanged, making the overall gain limited.
